about.title: About Us
about.missionText: The Enough Is Enough Foundation is dedicated to helping individuals overcome life's obstacles through faith, community support, and professional life coaching. We believe that transformation starts from within, and we are here to celebrate every step of your journey toward a better life.
about.overviewText: Founded on the principle that everyone deserves a chance to thrive, our foundation provides comprehensive programs for men and women seeking purpose, accountability, and community. Through grants and community contributions, we make our services accessible to those who need them most.

items.title: Men Of Hope
items.description: A comprehensive mentorship program empowering men to overcome challenges, build accountability, and discover their God-given purpose through community support and faith-based guidance.
items.longDescription: Men Of Hope is our flagship mentorship program designed specifically for men seeking purpose, accountability, and community. Through weekly sessions, one-on-one coaching, and group fellowship, participants build the foundation for lasting transformation.

items.title: How Much Do You Know
items.description: An educational initiative designed to expand knowledge, build awareness, and foster personal growth through interactive workshops and community learning experiences.
items.longDescription: How Much Do You Know challenges participants to expand their horizons through interactive workshops, community learning experiences, and awareness-building sessions that foster personal and collective growth.

items.title: When All of God's Children Gets Together
items.description: A unity-focused community program bringing people together across backgrounds to foster understanding, fellowship, and collective empowerment through faith.
items.longDescription: This unity-focused program brings people together across all backgrounds to foster understanding, fellowship, and collective empowerment. Through faith-centered gatherings and community events, we celebrate what happens when God's children come together.

items.title: Connecting to My RIB
items.description: A personal development program helping individuals connect with their inner strength, relationships, identity, and beliefs to build a foundation for lasting transformation.
items.longDescription: Connecting to My RIB helps individuals connect with their inner strength, Relationships, Identity, and Beliefs. This holistic program builds a foundation for lasting personal transformation through guided self-discovery.

items.title: Women Of Destiny
items.description: Empowering women to embrace their calling, overcome obstacles, and walk confidently into their destiny through mentorship, support groups, and faith-centered coaching.
items.longDescription: Women Of Destiny empowers women to embrace their calling and walk confidently into their destiny. Through mentorship circles, support groups, and faith-centered coaching, participants discover their purpose and overcome life's obstacles.

items.title: Housing for Men Of Hope
items.description: Providing safe, supportive housing solutions for men participating in the Men Of Hope program, creating a stable foundation for personal growth and community reintegration.
items.longDescription: Our Housing for Men Of Hope program provides safe, supportive housing for men in the Men Of Hope mentorship program. Stable housing creates the foundation needed for personal growth, accountability, and successful community reintegration.

boardMembers.name: Pastor Frank Bedford
boardMembers.title: President & Owner
boardMembers.bio:
Pastor Frank Bedford is a devoted husband, father, and man after God's own heart. He and his wife, Sharon, have five children — Jonquila, Serenia, Keshia, Kendall, and Travis — along with 14 grandchildren and 3 great-grandchildren.

A pastor for more than 20 years, Frank currently leads four congregations: Freewill Baptist Church (1st Sunday), New Zion Baptist Church (2nd Sunday), Oak Grove Baptist Church (3rd Sunday), and Bargeron Grove Baptist Church (4th Sunday), and works closely with Greenwood Baptist Church and several others. He also serves as an Assistant Moderator and stays active leading revivals and playing music, an area in which he has received numerous awards.

Frank attended school in Sylvania and works within the state prison system as a correctional officer, where he is well respected by the inmates he serves. He also serves as a counselor through the CGRA program and completed his training in Forsyth, Georgia.

Known for his humor as much as his seriousness about the Kingdom of God, Frank is a teacher, preacher, and musician who will never compromise God's Word. He loves to travel and has a heart for children. As President and Owner, Frank is leading the effort to establish Enough Is Enough Foundation as a fully recognized 501(c)(3) nonprofit serving the community.

boardMembers.name: Sharon Bedford
boardMembers.title: Assistant Director & Owner
boardMembers.bio:
Sharon has been married to Pastor Frank Bedford for 8 years. Together they have five children — Jonquila, Serenia, Keshia, Kendall, and Travis — 14 grandchildren, and 3 great-grandchildren.

God was not finished with Sharon yet. He allowed her to birth Enough Is Enough Foundation, which she and Frank are working to establish as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, and she is looking forward to serving the community.

Sharon is the author of “You Broke My Crayon” and a magazine titled “Brilliant.” She attended school throughout Statesboro before heading to Athens to study Criminal Justice at the University of Georgia. While there, she met her best friend, Benita, and became godmother to two beautiful girls, Taneka and Sharmeka.

Sharon has always kept a pen in her hand, believing words carry real power. Nearly 30 years ago she accepted Jesus Christ as her Lord and Savior and answered His calling on her life; she is a born-again, baptized believer known to many as Minister Sharon.

After two years in Athens, Sharon returned home due to a family emergency. She went on to spend 16 years at the Grinnell plant — known locally as “Big Nasty” — until it closed, then worked as a contractor for FedEx before returning to college. She later earned her Bachelor's degree in Criminal Justice from Grace Bible College Theological Seminary, receiving the gold key and the Delta Epsilon Tau emblem along the way.

Sharon is happily married to her soulmate, Frank, and together they lead Enough Is Enough Foundation as Owners.

boardMembers.name: Pastor Robert L. Johnson Jr.
boardMembers.title: Chair
boardMembers.bio:
Reverend Robert L. Johnson Jr. was raised in the admonition of the Lord by his mother, Mabel Johnson, and his father, the late Reverend R. L. Johnson Sr., who resided in Millen, Georgia. He received his high school education at E.C.I. in Twin City, Georgia.

Reverend Johnson served his country as a member of the United States Army. He is also deeply grateful for his position with the Appling County School System, which allows him to minister to young people from a variety of ethnic backgrounds. His wife of 14 years, Shanette A. Johnson, is also a teacher, at Metter Elementary School in Candler County, Georgia. Together they have five children — Raven (18), Robert III (25), Latavius (31), and Cortnei (32) — and five grandchildren.

Reverend Johnson is the pastor of Thankful New Jersey Missionary Baptist Church in Baxley, Georgia, a role he takes great pleasure in. A devotee of the Word and a well-read individual, he holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Theology from Andersonville Theological Seminary and a Master of Arts degree in Christian Studies from Luther Rice College and Seminary. He is currently pursuing a Doctor of Ministry in Leadership at Columbia International University.

Reverend Johnson is a meek servant of the Lord Jesus Christ who intends to maintain Jesus as the focal point of all his actions and words. He derives great satisfaction from his participation in community outreach and the dissemination of the Word of God to the people of God.

faqs.question: How do I enroll in a program?
faqs.answer: Contact us by phone at (855) 264-9103 or fill out our contact form. Our team will schedule an intake session to match you with the right program.

faqs.question: Are your services free?
faqs.answer: Many of our programs are funded through community contributions and grants. Contact us for pricing details — we work to make services accessible to all who need them.

faqs.question: What is life coaching with Sharon Bedford?
faqs.answer: Sharon provides professional faith-based life coaching focused on personal accountability, follow-through on commitments, and helping you walk into your God-given destiny.

faqs.question: Do you offer housing assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes! Our Housing for Men Of Hope program provides safe, supportive housing for men participating in the Men Of Hope mentorship program.

faqs.question: How can I support the foundation?
faqs.answer: You can support us through community contributions, volunteering, or spreading the word about our programs. Contact us to learn about partnership opportunities.
